source.title: Scaling Laws Revisited: Modeling the Role of Data Quality in Language Model Pretraining
source.authors: Anirudh Subramanyam; Yuxin Chen; Robert L. Grossman

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and formatting are flattened, but the experimental tables and relevant results are legible.
record.tranche_reason: It measures held-out loss across training-data volumes and fits a scaling law, using a quality-aware extension rather than reproducing the original scaling-law setup.
record.gate_note: The paper varies data volume and synthetic data quality while using one stated model configuration for each of its two text tasks. It does not sweep model size or compute, test a compute-optimal allocation, or test the other modalities and downstream claims. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Chinchilla-style parametric law, L = B/(D^β Q^γ) + E, to held-out loss. Each task uses one fixed model, with three data volumes per task: 0.1B, 1B and 10B tokens for CLM, and about 37M to 147M tokens for NMT. Its own results therefore bear on V1, but only along the data axis at fixed N. Because it compares Least Squares and Huber fits of β and E, they also bear on V7. The quality term Q is the paper's own extension and matches no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim that higher-quality data can substitute for model size and compute. They never vary N, so that claim rests on the assumed functional form rather than on measurement. They describe γ as stable at practical learning rates and treat it as an intrinsic task-dependent robustness index.
record.recipe_differences: Uses parametric scaling-law fitting similar to Hoffmann et al. but adds a data-quality factor, uses synthetic corruption and small fixed model configurations, and does not sweep parameter count or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted quality exponent differs by task and fitting method. The learning-rate sweep reports γ of 0.037 at 1e-5, 0.394 at 3e-4, 0.396 at 1e-3 and 0.177 at 5e-3; the authors call the last setting unstable and the first undertrained. CLM unseen-data fits also have different reported γ estimates from the in-distribution fits.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss rises with synthetic corruption at fixed D and N. The fitted quality exponent is sublinear and task-dependent: γ≈0.17–0.19 for NMT and ≈0.39–0.40 for CLM. It collapses at extreme learning rates (0.037 at 1e-5, 0.177 at 5e-3) and is ≈0.39 near 1e-3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data quality enters the scaling law as an effective-data multiplier Q^γ. The exponent γ is less than 1 and depends on task and noise type.

record.problems: Only one stated model configuration is used per task, so parameter-count and compute scaling are not tested. The quality variation is synthetic, the tested token ranges are limited, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated losses or fitted exponents despite using replicates. The unseen-data fits do not establish prediction for larger training runs.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 7 and 8 also report Q values 0.90, 0.80, 0.75, 0.70 and 0.60 for every replicate and data volume. Those 90 rows are omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; the retained Q=1.00 and Q=0.50 rows show the token-volume trend and clean-versus-noised endpoints, while fitted quality exponents are recorded in r37–r42. Figure-only contours and plots are not transcribed.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameter count and in compute. For NMT, the data axis spans only about 4x, not several orders of magnitude. With three D points per curve, a power law cannot be distinguished from other forms.
All of it. No small-run fit is used to predict much larger runs; the unseen-data fit changes the evaluation set, not the run scale.
All of it. N is never varied and there is no fixed-compute allocation.
All of it. Both tasks are text pretraining; NMT is a text task, not another modality or a fine-tuning regime.
All of it. No downstream tasks are measured.
Parameter counting, training schedule effects on β, data-source effects on the N/D split, and bending away from a power law. The learning-rate sweep reports γ only.

missing.what: Fitted data exponent β and floor E for each task and fitting method (CLM: β 0.395/0.396, E 3.44; NMT: β 0.263/0.250, E 0.147/0.067). These bear on V1's power-law form and on V7's fit-method dependence.
β and E fitted on unseen CLM evaluation data (β 0.397 LS and 0.391 Huber; E 4.55 vs 3.44)

record.verdict_notes: N is fixed for each task, so the A/N^α term is never estimated. The 'Chinchilla extension' is fitted only in D and Q. No uncertainties are reported despite three replicates, though replicate losses agree to within about 0.03. NMT's three data volumes span only a factor of 4.

versions.untested_parts: Tests loss against training-token count at fixed model configuration on CLM and NMT data; does not test scaling in parameter count or compute, or establish several orders of magnitude for those quantities.
Does not fit on small runs and predict loss for substantially larger runs. Its CLM unseen-data evaluation changes evaluation data, not run scale.
No fixed-compute sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is measured.
No architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Both experimental tasks use text; no image/video modality, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer experiment tests the stated generalisation.
No downstream task performance is measured.

Tests sensitivity of the quality exponent to task, fitting method and learning rate. Does not test parameter-counting conventions, compute-optimal allocation, or whether loss curves bend away from a single power law at larger scales.

relationships.condition: Data axis only, at a fixed small model. CLM spans 0.1B–10B tokens; NMT spans 37M–147M tokens. Three replicates, at both Q=1.00 and Q=0.50.
relationships.reason: Loss falls monotonically with D in every replicate: CLM 4.40→3.82→3.58 and NMT 1.85→1.57→1.35 at Q=1. A power law plus floor fits with β≈0.40 (CLM) and β≈0.25–0.26 (NMT); rows r1–r36.
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased in every replicate, including CLM 4.40→3.82→3.58 and NMT 1.85→1.57→1.35 at Q = 1, with fitted data exponents around 0.40 and 0.25–0.26 respectively.

relationships.condition: NMT, Least Squares vs Huber fit (Table 2)
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since no row records it. The floor E changes from 0.147 to 0.067 and β from 0.263 to 0.250 depending on fitting method.
relationships.display_finding: Changing from least-squares to Huber fitting moved the loss floor E from 0.147 to 0.067 and β from 0.263 to 0.250.

relationships.condition: CLM, Least Squares vs Huber fit and in-distribution vs unseen evaluation (Tables 2–3)
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since no row records it. β is essentially unchanged across fitting methods (0.395 vs 0.396) and across evaluation sets (0.397 and 0.391). E moves only with the evaluation data.
relationships.display_finding: β was 0.395 versus 0.396 across fitting methods and 0.397 versus 0.391 across evaluation sets, while E changed only with evaluation data.
